pr_title: Fix 'HeadOutlet' getting trimmed away for Blazor WebAssembly prerendered apps after publish
pr_body:
**Fix `HeadOutlet` getting trimmed away for Blazor WebAssembly prerendered apps after publish**
The `HeadOutlet` component was getting trimmed away in published ASP.NET Core hosted Blazor WebAssembly prerendered apps. This caused `<HeadContent>` and  `<PageTitle>` to take effect _only_ during prerendering.

**PR Description**
Added a `[DynamicDependency]` on `WebAssemblyHostBuilder.CreateDefault` to prevent `HeadOutlet` from getting trimmed away.

Fixes #35363

issue_context.title: Blazor: PreRender WASM: PageTitle/HeadContent not updated on publish
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
.Net 6 Preview 7
PageTitle and Head content does not update when navigating between pages after Publish.

> Note: It works as expected when developing (e.g. `dotnet run --project .\Server\`).

This is running WebAssembly PreRendering.

### To Reproduce
Repo to recreate
https://github.com/srpeirce/blazor-pagetitle-bug-net6-7

```
dotnet publish -c Release
Server\bin\Release\net6.0\publish\HeadFail.Server.exe
```

Open 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12847647/129493363-ff111f17-c774-4e28-a8a3-856bfd854355.png)

❌ Click Counter - Doesn't Update Page title
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12847647/129493396-4e54d00e-f67e-42b0-9b5a-f80366d8e3e5.png)

Additional:
Refreshing page, the title is updated.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12847647/129493416-15c50a9f-9d8e-4a80-aa02-a3fa42f59c39.png)

comments: @pranavkm this looks different - the fact that it's only breaking after publish suggests to me that something trickier is happening (plus, the updated templates aren't coming until RC1). I think I have an idea why is is happening from looking at the provided repro, but I will investigate it more thoroughly tomorrow.

review_comments:
Could I bother you to

a) Add the comment from your PR here?
b) Possibly update the WebAssembly pre-rendering scenario to include the HeadComponent?

The interesting thing is that the WebAssembly pre-rendering would run in to the same issue with all components in the framework if they happen to be root components. I can think of too many that would qualify for one, but it's something to be cognizant of when designing new ones. 


FYI @javiercn / @SteveSandersonMS

Since this type of bug could be possible with any arbitrary root component not referenced in the client-side build, I wonder if it could be worth it to throw a meaningful exception when a prerendered component type could not be found in its assembly. If we come up with an intuitive workaround, the exception message could also provide info about that.

>  if it could be worth it to throw a meaningful exception when a prerendered component type could not be found in its assembly

That seems like a good idea. We wouldn't have spent that long scratching our heads if things had failed noisily. @javiercn how do you feel about this? I imagine the change would be in the code that rehydrates from WebAssembly pre-rendering.

Agreed it would be good if we can do that.

We can afford a bit of extra overhead (for example, explicitly calling `Type.GetType` or whatever to see if we know about the type) in the code that rehydrates since it's a one-time cost during startup rather than being part of the core rendering loop.
